avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer; reduces lenvatinib concentrations and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue St. John's Wort; allow 2-week washout before lenvatinib initiation

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin-containing supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 induction significantly decreases lenvatinib levels
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; select alternative if antibiotic therapy needed

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate anticoagulant effects and increase bleeding risk with TKI therapy
avoid_supplements.action: Limit Vitamin E to <400 IU daily; monitor for bleeding signs

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibition may increase lenvatinib exposure
caution_supplements.action: Avoid grapefruit products; if used, monitor for increased adverse effects

caution_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild CYP3A4 induction at very high doses
caution_supplements.action: Moderate use acceptable; excessive supplementation should be avoided

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition increases lenvatinib bioavailability and toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Completely avoid grapefruit products during treatment

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase lenvatinib absorption; take on consistent basis with or without food
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent meal timing; counsel on uniform food intake patterns

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (excessive)
caution_foods.mechanism: May have mild CYP3A4 induction at very high chronic intake
caution_foods.action: Normal dietary intake acceptable; excessive supplementation should be limited

monitoring_notes: Monitor blood pressure weekly initially and regularly throughout therapy as lenvatinib commonly causes hypertension. Assess for signs of bleeding, proteinuria, hepatotoxicity, and QT prolongation; obtain baseline and periodic ECGs if risk factors present.
